title: Some 12-month pointing increased when the adult added new information
summary: In one experiment, 12-month-olds pointed on more trials when the adult's reply added information about the target than when the adult only shared attention.
body: Kovacs, Tauzin, Teglas, Gergely, and Csibra asked whether pointing can request information, not only share a feeling. In the first experiment, 32 monolingual 12-month-olds who pointed at least once saw puppets. After a point, either the adult shared attention and interest, or the adult also gave positive or negative information about the puppet. The share of trials with a point was higher after informing (mean 0.83) than after sharing only (mean 0.64). Infants who never pointed were excluded. The paper's claim is about this lab contrast. It does not replace the checklist ages for everyday pointing.

sources.title: Pointing as epistemic request: 12-month-olds point to receive new information
sources.author: Agnes M. Kovacs, Tibor Tauzin, Erno Teglas, Gyorgy Gergely, and Gergely Csibra
sources.note: Supports Experiment 1: 32 infants, higher pointing proportion in the informing condition (mean 0.83) than sharing (mean 0.64). Peer-reviewed open copy. Names paraphrased without diacritics.
